speaker: Teacher (concealment examined)
question: What is examined?
premises: tirobhāvasvarūpaṃ tu kathyamānaṃ vivicyatām — let the nature of concealment, as told, be examined.
svabhāvāt parameśāno niyatyaniyatikramam — from own nature the Lord touches the rule-bound and rule-free order: freedom includes both.
inference: Charter: examine concealment; the Lord's nature spans rule and rulelessness.

speaker: Teacher (self-willed Lord)
question: Why is he called self-willed?
premises: spṛśanprakāśate yena tataḥ svacchanda ucyate — touching, he shines forth; thereby he is called self-willed.
niyatiṃ karmaphalayorāśrityaiṣa maheśvaraḥ — having resorted to the rule of action and fruit, this Great Lord: freedom adopts rule.
inference: Named self-willed because, touching all, he shines — even resorting to rule.

speaker: Teacher (intermediate creation)
question: What does he ordain?
premises: sṛṣṭisaṃsthitisaṃhārānvidhatte 'vāntarasthitīn — creation, preservation, destruction he ordains — the intermediate states.
mahāsarge punaḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārānantyaśālini — and again, in the great creation, in the endlessness of creation-destruction.
inference: Three acts ordained intermediately; endless at the great scale.

speaker: Teacher (unforced stasis)
question: Does he abandon his form?
premises: ekaḥ sa devo viśvātmā niyatityāgataḥ prabhuḥ — one, that God, universe-self, the Lord arrived at abandoning rule.
avāntare yā ca sṛṣṭiḥ sthitiścātrāpyayantritam — and whatever intermediate creation — and stasis here too is unforced.
inference: The one Lord drops rule yet keeps form; intermediate stasis stays unforced.

speaker: Teacher (he does not abandon)
question: What is not abandoned?
premises: nojjhatyeṣa vapustyaktaniyatiśca sthito 'tra tat — he does not abandon the form; niyati-abandoned, standing here: that.
niyatyaiva yadā caiṣa svarūpācchādanakramāt — but by niyati alone, when through the self-concealing procedure.
inference: Form kept, rule dropped — yet rule may return as the concealing means.

speaker: Teacher (when the fruit-order applies)
question: When does karma-fruit apply?
premises: bhuṅkte duḥkhavimohādi tadā karmaphalakramaḥ — he enjoys suffering-delusion-and-the-rest: then the action-fruit order.
tyaktvā tu niyamaṃ kārmaṃ duḥkhamohaparītatām — but having abandoned the karmic restraint — enveloped in suffering-delusion.
inference: Karma-fruit binds only when the karmic restraint is kept; dropped, delusion envelops without fruit.

speaker: Teacher (awakened as unawakened)
question: How does the awakened behave?
premises: bibhāsayiṣurāste 'yaṃ tirodhāne 'napekṣakaḥ — desiring to shine forth, sits this one, in concealment disregardful.
yathā prakāśasvātantryāt pratibuddho 'pyabuddhavat — as, from light's freedom, the awakened like the unawakened.
inference: Freedom's play: the awakened sits as unawakened, disregardful in concealment.

speaker: Teacher (uncrossed as crossed)
question: How does he act?
premises: āste tadvadanuttīrṇo 'pyuttīrṇa iva ceṣṭate — so sits, uncrossed yet as-if-crossed, behaving.
yathā ca buddhastāṃ mūḍhaceṣṭāṃ kurvannapi dviṣan — and as the awake one her fool-conduct performing even while hating it.
inference: As-if-crossed conduct performed with inner hatred of it: freedom's theater.

speaker: Teacher (Vidyādhva's word)
question: What did the Vidyā-lord say?
premises: hṛdyāste mūḍha evaṃ hi prabuddhānāṃ viceṣṭitam — in the heart sits the fool: thus indeed of the awakened is the conduct.
śrīvidyādhipatiścāha mānastotre tadīdṛśam — and the venerable Vidyā-lord said in the Mānastotra such as this: lineage attests the paradox.
inference: The Mānastotra attests: awakened conduct looks foolish.

speaker: Teacher (Mānastotra: sun and lotus)
question: Who lacks appointment?
premises: ye yauṣmāke śāsanamārge kṛtadīkṣāḥ saṃgacchanto mohavaśādvipratipattim — who on your teaching-path, initiated, falling through delusion into dissent.
nūnaṃ teṣā nāsti bhavadbhānuniyogaḥ — surely of them there is not your sun-appointment.
saṅkocaḥ kiṃ sūryakaraistāmarasānām — can lotuses contract from sunbeams? Dissent proves non-appointment, as shadow proves no sun.
inference: The initiated dissenter lacks the sun-appointment: lotuses don't shrink from sunbeams.

speaker: Teacher (Mānastotra: wrong path)
question: What of the knowing who go wrong?
premises: jñātajñeyā dhātṛpadasthā api santo ye tvanmārgātkāpathagāste 'pi na samyak — known-and-knowable, creator-seated though being, who going wrong from your path, they too are not right.
prāyasteṣāṃ laiṅgikabuddhyādisamuttho mithyābodhaḥ sarpavasādīpajakalpaḥ — mostly of them, arisen from emblem-mind-and-the-rest, false awakening like snake-fat lamplight.
inference: Even the learned, straying, breed false awakening — snake-fat lamplight.

speaker: Teacher (Mānastotra: lead and nectar)
question: What of lead and undrunk nectar?
premises: yasmādviddhaṃ sūtakamukhyena nu tāmraṃ tadyadbhūyaḥ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ no samupeyāt — since pierced, with lead foremost: now copper — that which again to its own nature would not return.

no taiḥ pītaṃ bhūtalasaṃsthairamṛtaṃ tadyeṣāṃ tṛṭkṣudduḥkhavibādhāḥ punarasmin — nor drunk by earth-dwellers, that nectar of whom thirst-hunger-suffering-pains again herein: lead can't ungold; the undrunk stay thirsty.
inference: Lead pierced stays copper; nectar undrunk leaves thirst: states don't self-reverse.

speaker: Teacher (burning doubt)
question: What burns the awakened doubter?
premises: tataḥ prabuddhaceṣṭāsau mantracaryārcanādikā — then this awakened conduct — mantra-conduct-worship-and-the-rest.
dveṣeddhāntardahatyenaṃ dāhaḥ śaṅkaiva sā yataḥ — hate-kindled inwardly burns him; burning is doubt indeed — for.
inference: Doubt is the burn: hate-kindled inwardly, it consumes the doubter.

speaker: Teacher (not karma's might)
question: Did karma bring him here?
premises: na cāsya karmamahimā tādṛgyenetthamāsta saḥ — nor is it his past action's might such that thereby thus he has come.
kiṃ hi tatkarma kasmādvā pūrveṇātra samo vidhiḥ — indeed, what would that action be? Or why here would the procedure be the same as with the earlier?
inference: Concealment is not karmic payback: no deed explains it, no precedent binds it.

speaker: Teacher (the Lord's will deludes)
question: What deludes him?
premises: tasmātsā parameśecchā yayāyaṃ mohitastathā — hence that, the Lord's will, by which deluded, so.
anantakālasaṃvedyaduḥkhapātratvamīhate — endless-time-felt suffering-vesselhood he seeks: delusion aims at vesselhood.
inference: The Lord's will deludes him into seeking suffering-vesselhood.

speaker: Teacher (varied suffering)
question: Is suffering uniform?
premises: tatrāpi cecchāvaicitryādihāmutrobhayātmakaḥ — there too, if through will-variety, both-here-and-beyond-natured.
duḥkhasyāpi vibhedo 'sti ciraśaighryakṛtastathā — of suffering too there is division, made slow-or-swift, so.
inference: Suffering varies by will: here, hereafter, slow, swift.

speaker: Teacher (named sufferers)
question: Who suffers?
premises: kālakāmāndhakādīnāṃ paulastyapuravāsinām — of Kāla, Kāma, Andhaka and the rest, of Paulastya-city dwellers.
tathānyeṣāṃ tirobhāvastāvadduḥkho hyamutra ca — and of others: concealment — so much suffering, indeed hereafter too.
inference: Named sufferers: Kāla, Kāma, Andhaka, Laṅkā-dwellers, and the rest.

speaker: Teacher (samaya-violation concealment)
question: What second concealment?
premises: anyo 'pi ca tirobhāvaḥ samayollaṅghanātmakaḥ — another too is concealment, consisting in samaya-violation.
yaduktaṃ parameśena śrīmadānandagahvare — which was said by the Lord in the venerable Ānandagahvara: second kind, scripturally sourced.
inference: Second concealment: samaya-violation (Ānandagahvara).

speaker: Teacher (carrion-eaterhood)
question: What is its fruit?
premises: samayollaṅghanāddevi kravyādatvaṃ śataṃ samāḥ — from samaya-violation, O Goddess: carrion-eaterhood for a hundred years.
tatrāpi mandatīvrādibhedādbahuvidhaḥ kramaḥ — there too, through mild-intense-and-other-divisions, manifold is the course.
inference: Violation earns a hundred years as carrion-eater, graded mild-to-intense.

speaker: Teacher (grace returns)
question: Can the concealed return?
premises: svātantryācca maheśasya tirobhūto 'pyasau svayam — and through the Great Lord's freedom, though concealed, this one himself.
paradvāreṇa vābhyeti bhūyo 'nugrahamapyalam — through another's door, or comes back: again grace too, amply.
inference: Freedom re-admits: by oneself or another's door, grace returns amply.

speaker: Teacher (re-dīkṣā restores)
question: What restores Śiva-nature?
premises: bhūyo 'nugrahataḥ prāyaścittādyācaraṇe sati — and from renewed grace, expiation-and-the-rest being performed.
anusāreṇa dīkṣādau kṛte syācchivatāmayaḥ — accordingly, in initiation and the rest performed, he would be Śiva-natured.
inference: Expiation plus re-initiation restores Śiva-nature.

speaker: Teacher (post-mortem grace)
question: What if he died concealed?
premises: tirobhūtaḥ paretāsurapi — concealed, even the departed-breathed.
bandhusuhṛdgurūn ālambya śaktipātena dīkṣādyairanugṛhyate — kin, friends, teachers having resorted to, through śaktipāta, through initiations is graced.
inference: Even the concealed dead are graced through kin, teachers, śaktipāta.

speaker: Teacher (śaktipāta timing varies)
question: Does śaktipāta vary?
premises: tatrāpi kālaśīghratvaciratvādivibhedatām — there too, diversity of quick-slow-time and the rest.
tathaiti śaktipāto 'sau yenāyāti śivātmatām — so comes śaktipāta — it, by which he comes to Śiva-nature: timing varies, fruit constant.
inference: Śaktipāta varies in timing, not in fruit.

speaker: Teacher (five acts = Śiva-hood)
question: What is Śiva-hood?
premises: itthaṃ sṛṣṭisthitidhvaṃsatirobhāvamanugrahaḥ — thus creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment, grace.
iti pañcasu kartṛtvaṃ śivatvaṃ saṃvidātmanaḥ — in the five, doership is Śiva-hood, of consciousness-self.
inference: Doership in all five acts — including concealment — is Śiva-hood.

speaker: Teacher (ever-risen yogin)
question: What of the five-free yogin?
premises: pañcakṛtyasvatantratvasaṃpūrṇasvātmamāninaḥ — proud of five-act-freedom-complete-selfhood.
yogino 'rcājapadhyānayogāḥ saṃsyuḥ sadoditāḥ — the yogin's worship-japa-meditation-yogas, let them stand united, ever-risen (reading flagged).
inference: The five-free yogin's practices stand ever-risen.

speaker: Teacher (no magic shows)
question: Should he show off?
premises: aindrajālikavṛttānte na rajyeta kadācana — in magic-show business one should never delight.
sādāśivo 'pi yo bhogo bandhaḥ so 'pyucitātmanām — even Sadāśiva-enjoyment — which is bondage — that too, for the unfit.
inference: No delight in magic; even Sadāśiva-bliss binds the unfit.

speaker: Teacher (potter analogy)
question: Is doership primary?
premises: jñātṛtvameva śivatvaṃ svātantryaṃ tadihocyate — knowerness alone is Śiva-hood, is freedom: that is here called.
kulālavattu kartṛtvaṃ na mukhyaṃ tadadhiṣṭhiteḥ — like a potter, but, doership is not primary, from His superintendence (reading flagged).
inference: Knowerness, not potter-doership, is primary — superintended always.

speaker: Teacher (no refutation needed)
question: Must 'I am Śiva' be defended?
premises: iti jñātvā grahītavyā naiva jātvapi khaṇḍanā — thus having known, to be grasped: never at all, ever, refutation.
śivo 'haṃ cenmadicchānuvarti kiṃ na jagattviti — 'I am Śiva' — if following my will, why is not the world — thus the doubt: stated, not answered.
inference: No refutation needed; the objector's 'why not the world?' stands unanswered.

speaker: Teacher (may it flash)
question: What should flash?
premises: mamecchāmanuvartantāmityatrāhaṃvidi sphuret — 'let them follow my will' — here in the I-knower, may it flash.
śivo vā parameśāno dehādiratha nirmitaḥ — Śiva, or the Supreme Lord — body and the rest, then, fashioned.
inference: Let 'may they follow my will' flash in the I-knower; the fashioned body follows.

speaker: Teacher (whose body?)
question: Whose body proves what?
premises: śivasya tāvadastyetaddehastveṣa tathā tvayā — of Śiva, for now, is this — the body — but this, so.
kṛtaḥ kānyā dehatāsya tatkiṃ syādvācyatāpadam — fashioned by you: what other bodiness of his? Then what would be a speakable state?
inference: If you fashioned this body, what body proves Śiva? Unspeakable.

speaker: Teacher (toilers quoted)
question: Who toils?
premises: uktaṃ ca siddhasantānaśrīmadūrmimahākule — and told in the Siddhasantāna venerable Ūrmi-Mahākula.
pavanabhramaṇaprāṇavikṣepādikṛtaśramāḥ — wind-wandering-breath-scattering-and-the-rest-made toilers.
inference: The Ūrmi-Mahākula toilers: wind-wandering breath-scatterers.

speaker: Teacher (departure for liberation?)
question: Does departure liberate?
premises: kuhakādiṣu ye bhrāntāste bhrāntāḥ parame pade — in frauds and the rest, who deluded — they: deluded in the supreme state.
sarvatra bahumānena yāpyutkrāntirvimuktaye — everywhere with honor which even departure — for liberation: is departure honored everywhere as liberation?
inference: Question: is honored departure everywhere liberation?

speaker: Teacher (where would God go?)
question: Where could the all-pervading go?
premises: proktā sā sāraśāstreṣu bhogopāyatayoditā — taught she in the essence-śāstras, as enjoyment-means arisen.
yadi sarvagatā devo vadotkramya kva yāsyati — if all-pervading is God — tell! having departed, where will he go?
inference: If God is everywhere, departure goes nowhere: the utkrānti paradox.

speaker: Teacher (pot-like God?)
question: Is God partial?
premises: athāsarvagatastarhi ghaṭatulyastadā bhavet — but if not all-pervading, then pot-like then he would be.
utkrāntividhiyogo 'yamekadeśena kathyate — the departure-rite-yoga — this partially — is taught: partial teaching for a partial God?
inference: Dilemma: all-pervading (no departure) or pot-like (partial rite).

speaker: Teacher (partless, no departure)
question: How depart from the partless?
premises: niraṃśe śivatattve tu kathamutkrāntisaṃgatiḥ — but in the partless Śiva-principle, how departure-fittingness?
yathā dharādau vāyvante bhṛgvambvagnyupavāsakaiḥ — as from earth-and-the-rest to wind-end, by cliff-water-fire fasts (reading flagged).
inference: No departure fits the partless; cliff-water-fire fasts don't either.

speaker: Teacher (don't eject the soul)
question: Should the soul be ejected?
premises: ātmano yojanaṃ vyomni tadvadutkrāntivartanā — of the self joining in the void, likewise departure-procedure.
tasmānnotkramayejjīvaṃ paratattvasamīhayā — therefore one should not make the soul depart out of longing for the supreme principle.
inference: Don't eject the soul out of longing: prohibition of willed departure.

speaker: Teacher (Pūrvaśāstra's definition)
question: What did the Pūrvaśāstra define?
premises: śrīpūrvaśāstre tūktaṃ yadutkrānterlakṣaṇaṃ na tat — but in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra, whatever of departure the mark was told — not that.
muktyupāyatayā kiṃtu bhogahānyai tathaiṣaṇāt — as a means to liberation; but for loss of enjoyment, from such desiring: departure defined as enjoyment-loss, not liberation.
inference: Pūrvaśāstra: utkrānti defined for enjoyment-loss, not liberation.

speaker: Teacher (detached may leave)
question: Who may leave the body?
premises: japadhyānādisaṃsiddhaḥ svātantryācchaktipātataḥ — perfected by japa-meditation-and-the-rest, through freedom, from śaktipāta.
bhogaṃ prati viraktaśceditthaṃ dehaṃ tyajediti — toward enjoyment detached, if thus: the body should abandon — quoted permission.
inference: The detached perfected one may abandon the body: permission, not prescription.

speaker: Teacher (Bhīṣma precedent)
question: What of Bhīṣma?
premises: svacchandamṛtyorapi yad bhīṣmādeḥ śrūyate kila — even of self-willed death, what from Bhīṣma onward is heard, indeed.
bhogavairasyasaṃprāptau jīvitāntopasarpaṇam — on arrival at enjoyment-distaste: approaching life's end.
inference: Bhīṣma precedent: self-willed death on enjoyment-distaste.

speaker: Teacher (siddhi-body stays)
question: Can the siddhi-body be shed?
premises: yogamantrāmṛtadravyavarādyaiḥ siddhibhāktanuḥ — by yoga-mantra-nectar-substance-boon-and-the-rest, a siddhi-partaking body.
hātuṃ nahyanyathā śakyā vinoktakramayogataḥ — to abandon: for not otherwise is possible without the stated-sequence-practice.
inference: The siddhi-made body can't be shed except by the stated sequence.

speaker: Teacher (deem enjoyment ugly)
question: What does the Mālinītantra add?
premises: uktaṃ ca mālinītantre parameśena tādṛśam — and told in the Mālinītantra by the Supreme Lord likewise.
sarvamapyathavā bhogaṃ manyamāno virūpakam — all even — or else — enjoyment deeming ugly: deem all enjoyment ugly.
inference: Mālinītantra: deem all enjoyment ugly — the same doctrine.

speaker: Teacher (freedom taught in duties)
question: What is the teaching?
premises: ityādi vadatā sarvairalakṣyāntaḥsatattvakam — 'thus and the rest,' by one who says: by all, the inner-reality-unseen reality (provisional).
evaṃ sṛṣṭyādikartavyasvasvātantryopadeśanam — thus: teaching of one's own freedom in creation-and-the-rest duties.
inference: The teaching: one's own freedom in all duties, reality unseen by all.

speaker: Teacher (chief dīkṣā)
question: What is the chief initiation?
premises: yatsaiva mukhyadīkṣā syācchiṣyasya śivadāyinī — which very chief initiation should be of the disciple, Śiva-giving.
uktaṃ śrīniśicāre ca bhairavīyeṇa tejasā — told in the venerable Niśicāra, and by Bhairavī energy, radiance.
inference: Chief dīkṣā: the freedom-teaching, Śiva-giving, Bhairavī-radiant.

speaker: Teacher (thought-free beholds)
question: Who beholds the pervaded universe?
premises: vyāptaṃ viśvaṃ prapaśyanti vikalpojjhitacetasaḥ — pervaded, the universe they behold: the thought-abandoned-minded.
vikalpayuktacittastu piṇḍapātācchivaṃ vrajet — but the thought-joined-minded: from body's fall, Śiva reaches.
inference: Thought-free behold now; thought-bound reach Śiva at death.

speaker: Teacher (jīvanmukta now)
question: Who is liberated alive?
premises: bāhyadīkṣādiyogena caryāsamayakalpanaiḥ — by outer-initiation-and-the-rest-practice, through conduct-samaya-constructs.
avikalpastathādyaiva jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ — thought-free, just so, now indeed: living-liberated, no doubt.
inference: Thought-free now: living-liberated, no doubt.

speaker: Teacher (fire-mass blazes)
question: What blazes at the end?
premises: saṃsārajīrṇatarumūlakalāpakalpasaṃkalpasāntaratayā — by thought made like the root-mass of the world-worn-out tree, inwardly.

paramārthavahneḥ syurvisphuliṅgakaṇikā api cettadante dedīpyate vimalabodhahutāśarāśiḥ — of the ultimate fire: may there be spark-fragments; even if at its end, blazes intensely the pure-awakening-fire-mass.
inference: Even spark-fragments of the burnt world-tree blaze into the pure-awakening-fire-mass.

speaker: Teacher (approach shown)
question: What closes?
premises: itthaṃ dīkṣopakramo 'yaṃ darśitaḥ śāstrasaṃmataḥ — thus the initiation-approach, this, shown, scripturally approved: colophon.
inference: Colophon: the initiation-approach shown, scriptures concurring.
